cues.en: of what it is that's going on in order to be able to achieve your goal. cues.en: So let's try to understand what that is. So let's start to talk about what is the design ideal of functional programming. Well, in functional programming, we really like these things called pure functions. And why do we like pure functions? It also turns out they're easy to test for reasons that I'll explain later.
cues.zh: 所以我们来探究一下其中的缘由。先来聊聊函数式编程的设计理想是什么。在函数式编程中，我们非常推崇纯函数。为什么喜欢纯函数？因为它们容易推导、容易操作、容易组合，并且具备各种优秀的特质。而且事实证明它们还很容易测试，原因我稍后会讲。

cues.en: So we really like our pure functions. That is the design ideal of a functional programming code base. So what is a pure function? We need to understand that. A pure function is a function, first of all, that is deterministic. It always returns the same output if you give it the same input. The other thing about a pure function is that it has no side effects.
cues.zh: 所以我们非常喜欢纯函数。这就是函数式代码库的设计理想。那么什么是纯函数呢？我们得搞清楚。首先，纯函数是确定性的。只要输入相同，输出就必然相同。其次，纯函数没有副作用。

cues.en: A side effect may be that you send an email. It may be that you write files to disk. You delete a record from a database. It may also just be that you change a value in memory. So it might not be something that involves IO. But anything that is observable from outside of the function, if it changes the state of something outside of the function, we call that a side effect.
cues.zh: 副作用可能是发了封邮件，可能是往磁盘写了文件，或是从数据库删了条记录。它也可能只是修改了内存中的某个值，并不一定涉及 I/O 操作。但只要是函数外部可观察到的任何行为，只要它改变了函数外部的状态，我们就称之为副作用。

cues.en: So it needs to do neither of those. It can't do side effects, it can't do non-determinism. If it's deterministic, has no side effect, we call it a pure function. So you probably go then, but side effects, all software development is basically all about doing side effects. When we create software, we want to print...
cues.zh: 所以它这两者都不能做。不能有副作用，也不能有非确定性。如果它是确定性的、没有副作用，我们称它为纯函数。那你可能会说，可是副作用——所有软件开发基本上都是在做副作用。我们开发软件时，想要打印……

cues.en: new UI on the screen of the user. That's a side effect. We want to send off emails. That's a side effect. We want to put things into a database. That's a side effect. How would we ever be able to do something if we can only do pure functions? And we never say that you can only do pure functions. We just say, we like pure functions, so we want to maximize how many pure functions we have. But we absolutely acknowledge that we also need to have impure functions because we need to write to database.
cues.zh: 在用户屏幕上显示新的 UI。那是副作用。我们想发邮件。那是副作用。我们想把东西写进数据库。那是副作用。如果只能用纯函数，我们怎么可能做成任何事？我们从没说过只能用纯函数。我们只是说，我们喜欢纯函数，所以想尽可能多地拥有纯函数。但我们完全承认，也需要有非纯函数，因为我们要写数据库。

cues.en: basis, we need to update your user interface and we need to do all of those things. We just say, we prefer the pure functions because they're easier to develop, they're easier to maintain. So there's a couple of relationship between those two things that you need to understand. First of all, if you have a pure function and you want to call another pure function from that pure function, that is absolutely OK. You can do that. It doesn't make your calling pure function more or less pure that it calls another pure function. That's just a way of composing things.
cues.zh: 在此基础上，我们需要更新用户界面，还需要做所有这些事。我们只是说，更喜欢纯函数，因为它们更容易开发、更容易维护。所以你需要理解这两者之间的几种关系。首先，如果你有一个纯函数，并想从这个纯函数中调用另一个纯函数，那完全没问题。你可以这么做。它调用另一个纯函数，并不会让你这个发出调用的纯函数变得更纯或更不纯。这只是一种组合事物的方式。

cues.en: makes absolutely sense. If you have an impure function and you want to call another impure function from that impure function, you can absolutely do that. It doesn't change whether it's more or less impure.
cues.zh: 这完全说得通。如果你有一个非纯函数，并想从这个非纯函数中调用另一个非纯函数，你完全可以这么做。这不会改变它变得更非纯还是更不非纯。

cues.en: That's possible. You can also call a pure function from an impure function. If the function is already impure, it doesn't become more or less impure by calling for pure functions. And a pure function is something as simple as 2 plus 2. So you can definitely do 2 plus 2 equals 4, even though you're in an impure context, you're trying to save something into the database. That's absolutely possible. Going the other way, on the other hand, is not possible.
cues.zh: 这是可能的。你也可以从非纯函数中调用纯函数。如果一个函数已经非纯，它不会因为调用纯函数而变得更非纯或更不非纯。纯函数可以简单到 2 加 2。所以你完全可以在非纯上下文里做 2 加 2 等于 4，即使你正试图把某些东西保存到数据库。这完全可能。反过来则不行。

cues.en: And there are various ways it's not possible. In Haskell, for example, it wouldn't even compile. I'll show you what that looks like in a moment. In F sharp, it's not that you can't...
cues.zh: 而且它无法做到的方式有多种。例如在 Haskell 里，甚至根本无法通过编译。我稍后会给你展示那是什么样子。在 F# 里，并不是说你不能……

cues.en: sort of do it if you imagine that you have a function that's pure at the moment but then you want to change the implementation a little bit and the change you introduce is a call to an impure function. What's actually going to happen then is it will compile but that, you know, your function that was, you know, pure before now also becomes impure because it's calling into another impure function. So it just, you know, moves from one place to the other one, you could say. So you can't go the other way. You can't call impure code from pure code. That's really important.
cues.zh: 某种程度上做到它：如果你想象你有一个目前是纯的函数，但随后你想稍微改一下实现，而你引入的改动是调用一个非纯函数。实际会发生的是，它能编译，但你之前那个纯函数现在也变成了非纯函数，因为它在调用另一个非纯函数。所以可以说，它只是从一个位置移到了另一个位置。因此你不能反过来。你不能从纯代码调用非纯代码。这一点非常重要。

cues.en: Let's try to see an example of what that would look like and why that is important. Because this is basically the explanation for why we tend to fall into this ports and adapters architecture when we do functional programming. Right. OK. So let's look at an example. So one of my favorite examples is a scenario where you try to implement a system for doing restaurant reservations. So you know these exist already. But this is just to, you know, it's a nice, rich problem domain. So it's nice to talk about.
cues.zh: 我们来看个例子，感受一下它是什么样的，以及为什么这很重要。因为这基本上解释了为什么我们在做函数式编程时，往往会自然采用这种端口与适配器架构。对吧。好的。那我们来看个例子。我最喜欢的例子之一，就是实现一个餐厅预订系统。大家都知道这种系统早就有了。但这是因为，你知道，它是一个非常典型且丰富的业务场景，很适合拿来讨论。

cues.en: So you imagine that you want to make a reservation on a restaurant. You go to a website or an app, fill in some details, and then you hit a button to send off your reservation. And in this particular scenario, what we can imagine then is that there's a JSON document that your user interface somehow posts to an HTTP-based server. And the HTTP-based server receives that JSON document and wants to deal with it. So we'll go through five steps here. The first thing we need to do is to validate the incoming JSON, because JSON is not particularly strongly typed.
cues.zh: 设想你要在一家餐厅预订座位。你打开网站或 App，填写一些信息，然后点击按钮提交预订。在这个特定场景中，我们可以设想用户界面会以某种方式向基于 HTTP 的服务器发送一个 JSON 文档。基于 HTTP 的服务器收到该 JSON 文档后需要对其进行处理。这里我们分为五步。首先需要验证传入的 JSON，因为 JSON 并不是特别强类型的。

cues.en: So we'll need to validate, is it actually well formed? Do we understand what is being said here?
cues.zh: 所以我们需要验证：它的格式到底是否规范？我们能理解其中的含义吗？

cues.en: If it's valid, we can move on. If it's invalid, we'll need to return a response. We'll get back to that later on. But imagine that we've determined that this is a valid, well-formed JSON document. It means we understand what it's trying to say. It means we understand the date on which the reservation is being attempted. That means also we'll need to look into our database to say, how many existing reservations do we already have for that date? How many reserved seats do we have from that date?
cues.zh: 如果验证通过，就可以继续。如果无效，我们就需要返回一个响应，这个稍后再说。但假设我们已经确认这是一个有效且格式规范的 JSON 文档。这意味着我们理解了它的意图，也知道了用户想要预订的日期。这也意味着我们需要查询数据库：那天我们已经有多少预订了？那天已经预订了多少个座位？

cues.en: from that date. Let's read that from the database. Now we have enough information to make a business decision. Do we actually have enough excess capacity to accept the reservation? If we have, we can save the reservation into the database so that it becomes part of the decision when the next request comes in.
cues.zh: 关于那个日期，我们从数据库读取这些信息。现在我们有了足够的信息来做出业务决策：我们到底有没有足够的剩余空位来接受这次预订？如果有，我们就可以把预订保存到数据库中，以便在下一个请求到来时作为决策依据。

cues.en: We might be short-circuiting in various steps here, because if we can't validate, there's no reason to go through the rest. If we decide that we can't accept the reservation, there's no reason to save it into the database. So we might short-circuit at various points, but I'm not showing those arrows. But what we might want to do anyway, independent of the decision we reach, we want to say, well, let's translate our decision back into an HTTP response that can then be sent back to the client.
cues.zh: 在这些步骤中我们可能会提前短路返回，因为如果验证失败，就没必要继续后面的步骤了。如果我们决定不能接受预订，也就没必要存入数据库。所以我们可能会在不同节点提前返回，不过我这里没有画出那些流程箭头。但无论做出什么决策，我们最终都要把决策结果转换回 HTTP 响应，然后发送回客户端。

cues.en: So those are the five steps that we need to go through. And you'll notice that three of them are green, and three of them are not red, but purple. And the three, obviously, are the pure functions, and the purple ones are the impure functions. But you'll also notice that they're sort of interleaved. So we have those three pure functions, and we have those two impure functions. And we somehow need to mix them together, and we'll wonder how we can do that.
cues.zh: 这就是我们需要经历的五个步骤。你会注意到其中三个是绿色的，另外两个不是红色的，而是紫色的。显然，绿色的三个是纯函数，紫色的是不纯函数。但你也会发现它们是交替出现的。我们有三个纯函数，两个不纯函数。我们需要把它们结合在一起，那么问题来了，我们该怎么做呢？

cues.en: So let's try to look at what that would look like. So I'm going to show you some Haskell code. And I'm not assuming that you know Haskell at all. What's really important here is just the top line. So actually, everything but the top line is the only reason why. So the top line is the function declaration and its type. And the rest of it is actually the implementation of the function, all the whites and so on beneath that. And you don't really need to read that. Just read the top line here. I just put the other function body there to show off that.
cues.zh: 那我们来试着看看那会是什么样子。接下来我会给你看一些 Haskell 代码。我完全不假设你懂 Haskell。这里真正重要的是顶行。其实，除了顶行之外的内容都只是陪衬。顶行是函数声明及其类型。其余部分才是函数实现，包括下面那些细节。你其实不用读它们，只看顶行就行。我把另一个函数体放那儿只是为了炫一下。

cues.en: I can actually write Haskell code. But it's not important. Let's look at the top line there, the validate reservation, the blue and the orange stuff here. So validate reservation just declares, here's a function, its name is validate reservation. The orange stuff then is the type of the function. It takes something called reservation rendition as input. This is sort of our Haskell representation of the JSON document. It returns something called either error reservation as output. It's not particularly important exactly what that means. What's important here to realize
cues.zh: 我确实能写 Haskell 代码，但这不重要。看这里的顶行，validate reservation，还有蓝色和橙色的部分。validate reservation 只是声明：这里有个函数，名字叫 validate reservation。橙色部分则是函数的类型。它接收一个叫 reservation rendition 的东西作为输入。这算是我们用 Haskell 表示 JSON 文档的方式。它返回一个叫 either error reservation 的东西作为输出。它具体是什么意思并不特别重要。这里真正要意识到的是——

cues.en: is that this function is pure, and it's guaranteed by the compiler to be pure. Why? How do we know that? Well, basically because in Haskell, all functions are pure by default. So unless explicitly stated otherwise, they are pure. And this one does not explicitly state that it's impure, and therefore it's pure. And because the type is declared as being pure, if I tried to do something in the function body there that was impure, it wouldn't compile.
cues.zh: 这个函数是纯的，而且编译器保证它是纯的。为什么？我们怎么知道？基本上因为 Haskell 里所有函数默认都是纯的。除非显式说明，否则它们都是纯的。这个函数没有显式声明自己不纯，所以它就是纯的。而且因为类型被声明为纯的，如果我试图在函数体里做不纯的事，就编译不过。

cues.en: But I'm not trying to do something impure in the function body there. So this compiles, and it's fine. Now, what does it look like if we want to explicitly state that a function is impure? Well, it looks like this. So I'm just going to show you a function declaration without its implementation. So this is the next function in that little sequence diagram that I showed you. Get reserve seeds from DB.
cues.zh: 但我没打算在函数体里做不纯的事。所以它能编译，没问题。那如果我们想显式声明一个函数不纯，会是什么样？是这样的。我只给你看一个没有实现的函数声明。这是我之前展示的时序图里的下一个函数：Get reserve seeds from DB。

cues.en: So it takes a connection string and a sown time. That's basically just a representation of the date. And then it returns something called IO of int. And this is impure. And the reason why we know that is because those two letters, IO, indicates that this is an impure function. So basically, what is it returning? IO of int is just an integer. So it returns the number of already reserved seeds for that sown time. But that integer originates from an impure context.
cues.zh: 它接收一个连接字符串和一个播种时间。后者基本上就是日期的表示。然后它返回一个叫 IO of int 的东西。这就是不纯的。我们知道它不纯，是因为那两个字母 IO 表明这是不纯函数。所以它到底返回什么？IO of int 就是一个整数。它返回该播种时间下已预订的种子数。但这个整数来自一个不纯上下文。

cues.en: Because it's not deterministic. Reading from a database is not deterministic. You could read from a database, calling the same database query twice, and you'll get two different results because the state of the database changed in the meantime. So that's not deterministic. So that is an impure operation. But basically, what IO of int says is that there is an integer, but it's packaged up inside of an impure context. So you can almost think about this impure context as being sort of like a little bubble or a little space that
cues.zh: 因为它不是确定性的。读数据库不是确定性的。同一个数据库查询调两次，可能得到两个不同结果，因为期间数据库状态变了。所以它不是确定性的。所以这是不纯操作。但 IO of int 基本上是在说：这里有个整数，但它被打包在一个不纯上下文里。你几乎可以把这不纯上下文想成一个小气泡或小空间，

cues.en: that sort of sits around that integer. And when you're outside, when you're in a pure context, you can see the bubble or box or whatever you want to call it where that integer is inside. But you can't see what the integer is. So it's a little bit like Schrodinger's cat, maybe. I don't know. Not really. But anyway, so you know that you have something that contains an integer. But as long as you're in a pure context, you don't know what that integer is. So how do we get that integer? I'll get back to that. But I talked about how you can't
cues.zh: 它围绕着那个整数。当你在外面，在纯上下文里时，你能看到那个气泡或盒子——随便怎么叫——整数就在里面。但你看不到这个整数是什么。所以这也许有点像薛定谔的猫。我不知道，也不太像。但总之，你知道自己有个包含整数的东西。可只要你在纯上下文里，你就不知道这个整数是什么。那我们怎么拿到这个整数？我后面再说。但我之前讲过，你不能

cues.en: call an impure function from a pure function. But I'd like my business logic to be impure, because basically I just like as much as possible of my code to be pure. So I want to be able to make a decision. So I could write a new function called checkCapacity. And if I just for a moment forget about this distinction between pure and impure, I could say, well, in my ideal dream world, I'd like to have an integer which represents the number of already-reserved seeds.
cues.zh: 从纯函数里调用不纯函数。但我希望业务逻辑是不纯的，因为基本上我希望代码尽可能多部分是纯的。所以我希望能做决定。那我可以写一个新函数叫 checkCapacity。如果我暂时忘掉纯和不纯的区别，我可以说，在我理想的梦里，我想要一个整数，表示已预订的种子数。

cues.en: And I also need an integer that represents the capacity of the restaurant. So that might be just another number. The restaurant can hold 10 people, or it can hold 100 people, or whatever. So I need those numbers. And then I also need the reservation itself. If I have those three pieces of information, I can make a decision. That is a pure function. How do we know that? Because there's no IO involved in the type declaration there.
cues.zh: 我还另外需要一个表示餐厅容量的整数。那可能就是另一个数字。餐厅可以容纳 10 个人，或者 100 个人之类的。所以我需要这些数字。接着我还需要预约信息本身。只要掌握了这三条信息，我就可以做出决定。这是一个纯函数。我们怎么知道呢？因为类型声明里完全没有涉及 IO。

cues.en: So I'm sort of just brushing aside that I don't actually have an int for the reserve Cs. I have an IO of int. So how do I get it out? Well, I'll get back to that, but it turns out to be possible. But if I did that, though, if I decide to accept the reservation, I could say, well, all right, let's save the reservation into the database again. Now that is another impure operation. We can see that because it returns IO of
cues.zh: 所以，我有点在回避一个事实，那就是我实际上并没有拿到已预约座位的 int。我拿到的是一个 IO of int。那怎么把它取出来呢？这个我稍后再讲，但事实证明这是可行的。但如果我做到了，并决定接受预约，我就可以说，好吧，我们把预约再次保存到数据库中。这又是一个非纯操作。我们可以看出这一点，因为它返回的是 IO of

cues.en: Nothing. Those empty brackets there, we call those unit. And both fsharp and Haskell has this thing called unit. And it's basically void like it ought to be, because unit is a real value. So you can use unit as a return value, but you also use it as input. So you can take a return value and pass it on as input to another function if you need to do that. And that turns out to sometimes be interesting to do. But if you think about those...
cues.zh: Nothing。那一对空括号，我们称之为 unit。F# 和 Haskell 都有这个叫做 unit 的东西。它基本上就是本该如此的 void，因为 unit 是一个真实的值。所以你可以把 unit 作为返回值，也可以把它作为输入。如果你需要的话，你可以拿一个返回值，把它作为输入传递给另一个函数。有时这么做会很有意思。但如果你把那些……

cues.en: empty brackets as being sort of the same thing as void in C sharp or Java, you know that if you have a method in C sharp or Java that returns void, it pretty strongly indicates that there must be a side effect of calling that method. Because why would you call a method that doesn't return anything? You probably want to achieve some sort of side effect. So that's possible also in Haskell, but it's only possible to have side effects.
cues.zh: 空括号看作类似于 C# 或 Java 中的 void，你就知道，在 C# 或 Java 里如果一个方法返回 void，那它极大概率意味着调用该方法必然会产生副作用。因为谁会去调用一个什么都不返回的方法呢？你肯定想达成某种副作用。在 Haskell 中这也是可能的，但产生副作用的前提……

cues.en: in an impure context, because side effects are per definition impure, so we have IO of unit. Now, the final thing we need to do is to say, well, if we've reached a decision so far, we want to translate it back to an HTTP result, so we could do that as well.
cues.zh: 只能是在非纯上下文中，因为根据定义副作用就是非纯的，所以我们得到了 IO of unit。现在，我们最后要做的是，如果目前已经做出了决定，我们想把它转换回 HTTP 结果，我们也可以这么做。

cues.en: Again, you just look at the top line there. We can see there's no IO involved in that, so that's a pure function as well. This is just a translation from our internal representation of did we accept the reservation or not, and then just something that we can translate to HTTP responses that can go on the wire. That's basically what we're doing here. All right, so we have those five functions. I wrote...
cues.zh: 同样，只要看最上面那一行。我们能看到它不涉及 IO，所以这也是一个纯函数。这只是把我们内部表示的“是否接受预约”，转换成可以通过网络传输的 HTTP 响应。基本上我们在这里做的就是这个。好的，现在我们有了这五个函数。我写了……

cues.en: three pure functions, two impure functions, I somehow need to interleave those so that they can all talk together because I need some of the impure information in order to continue with some of the pure operations. But I said I can't call impure functions from pure functions. So how do I resolve that issue? Well, it turns out that at the boundary of the system, every system is impure because
cues.zh: 三个纯函数，两个非纯函数，我得想办法把它们交织在一起，让它们能够相互沟通，因为我需要一些非纯信息来继续进行某些纯操作。但我说过，不能从纯函数中调用非纯函数。那我该怎么解决这个问题呢？事实证明，在系统的边界上，每个系统都是非纯的，因为……

cues.en: you know, when you get a request coming into a system or someone presses a button on a user interface or whatever, that is non-deterministic side-effective behavior anyway. So everything that happens, you know, at the entry point of a system is by definition impure anyway. So we could imagine that we have some sort of entry point where you could say, well, if we put all of those functions into some sort of web framework,
cues.zh: 要知道，当有请求进入系统，或者有人在用户界面上按下了按钮之类的，这横竖都是不确定且有副作用的行为。所以无论如何，发生在系统入口处的一切，按定义都是非纯的。所以我们可以设想有某种入口，你可以说，好吧，如果我们把所有这些函数放到某种 Web 框架中，

cues.en: We could imagine that we have some sort of framework that contains a dispatcher and it says, well, all right, here's a JSON document that arrives at this particular URL. It ought to be dispatched to a function that can deal with that. And that is an impure function. So we need to have an impure function that can deal with an incoming request anyway. So let's use that function to compose all of those other things together. So in this case, I've just called it post-reservation.

cues.zh: 如果人们刚接触企业级开发，刚大学毕业，或者刚从任何学面向对象设计的地方出来，他们很可能一上手就做出这样的设计。他们会说：我需要在系统里跟踪用户。我的系统里有很多用户。用户有 ID，有一个 ID，还有一个用户名。我还需要把用户持久化到数据库里。所以我会做创建、读取、更新和删除，让它们能和我的数据库通信。

cues.en: This is a well-described design pattern. It's called Active Record. And if you read Martin Fowler's book, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture, it's actually described in that book. So it almost seems like this is some sort of well-known good thing.

cues.en: that is actually not a good way to design systems. cues.zh: 这其实并不是一个设计系统的好方法。尽管这看起来非常面向对象——用户对象封装了用户数据以及属于该用户的所有行为。这看起来很符合面向对象。从原则上讲，这并没有错。但问题在于，你会说：

cues.en: I need to do things with users. And later on, you figure out I need to do other things with users as well, because I want to be able to send an email to a user. So I'll also add that feature to the user object. And what often happens with these things is that the more...
cues.zh: 我需要对用户做一些操作。随后你又发现，我还需要对用户做其他操作，比如我想能给用户发邮件。于是我也把这个功能加到了用户对象里。而这类事情通常的走向是：

cues.en: behavior you add to a class like this, the more behavior it also attracts. So you'd end up with a couple of very, very big classes in a typical source code base, where the classes just attract more and more of this sort of behavior, and they become less and less cohesive. cues.zh: 你给这样的类添加的行为越多，它吸引而来的行为也就越多。结果就是在典型的源码库中，最终会出现几个非常庞大的类，它们不断吸引越来越多的这类行为，内聚性也越来越差。我们最终把那些庞大的类称为“上帝类”（God class），这也是个众所周知的反模式。所以我们吃尽苦头才明白，这其实会导致

cues.en: There's this book called Domain Driven Design by Eric Evans. And it's sort of like two books in one. cues.en: And these are the objects that you learn about in university and so on. cues.en: And we know that that's not really true, but there's some truth in that. Some of the nouns will actually be some of the entities you're interested in. Entities are objects that have, you know,

cues.zh: 类型声明，但它不包含任何行为。当然，在 F# 里你也可以添加行为，因为 F# 是所谓的多范式语言，如果你想的话，完全可以把它写得更面向对象，但你大可不必非要这么做。这样挺好，这也是它所推崇的。比如在 Haskell 中，语法虽然略有不同，但本质概念是一样的，而且在 Haskell 里你根本没法给数据添加任何行为。数据就是数据。

cues.zh: 所以这基本上就是 F# 想让你做的，也是 Haskell 想让你做的。它想让你做的事，正是 Eric Evans 花了400页试图教你的东西；基本上如果你学过 Haskell，或者学过 F#——你知道 F# 的函数式部分——这就是你该做的。这就是语言引导你去做的事。所以你又一次掉进了“成功之坑”。它们会说，嗯，这两件事不该混在一起，它们应该分开，但它们可以互相配合，这样完全没问题。

cues.zh: 那么我们来聊聊可测试性吧，因为可测试性总是很有趣的话题。Kent Beck 在90年代中期提出了测试驱动开发的概念，大概是95、96年左右，确切日期我记不清了。当时他刚开始搞这个的时候，争议非常非常大。而我大约是在2003年接触到测试驱动开发的，那时候它的争议依然非常大。现在大家对测试驱动开发的接受度更高了，甚至到了大多数人都觉得它本该如此的程度。

cues.en: you know, that's actually, you know, a well-known best practice now. But it turns out it's still sort of controversial. cues.zh: 你知道，现在这其实已经成了人尽皆知的最佳实践。但事实证明，它依然带有一点争议。而且时不时地，这种争议又会重新冒出来。比如几年前，David Heinemeier Hansson 写了一篇文章，题为《TDD 已死，测试长存》。

cues.en: And basically what he, I'll try to cover what he said in a moment, but basically he said, well, it's not that he's against testing, but he just thinks that test driven developments actually leads to a lot of problems. He leads to what he calls test induced damage.
cues.zh: 他大体的意思——我稍后会详细讲讲他说了什么——但基本上他说，并不是他反对测试，而是他认为测试驱动开发实际上会导致很多问题。它会导致他所谓的“测试引起的损伤”。

cues.en: Now, David Hye and Maya Hansen can be quite controversial to himself and some people really don't like his style because he's swearing a lot and he's saying things in a very provocative manner. But I've found over the years that if you actually try to listen to what it is that he's trying to say to you, he's really a free thinking spirit. He does not just go with the flow. He goes against the grain and sometimes it seems like he makes an effort out of doing that. But basically, if he says something that goes against the grain,
cues.zh: 话说回来，David Heinemeier Hansson 本人也挺有争议的，有些人真的很不喜欢他的风格，因为他经常爆粗口，说话极具挑衅性。但这些年来我发现，如果你真的试着去听他到底想表达什么，你会发现他确实是个特立独行的人。他绝不随波逐流，总是反其道而行之，有时甚至像是在故意这么做。但基本上，只要他说了什么逆耳之言，

cues.en: It's worth the effort at least to try to understand what it is he says because he's a very intelligent young man. I can say young man now because my hair is gray. So let's try to understand what it is that he says. He says test room development leads to test induced damage. That is his claim. I'm not saying it's my claim. That is his claim. Let's try to understand what he means by test induced damage. So here is a class called capacity checker that tries to check the capacity of one of these restaurant reservation system.
cues.zh: 至少值得花点心思去理解他到底在说什么，因为他是个非常聪明的年轻人——我现在可以叫他年轻人了，毕竟我都满头白发了。所以让我们试着理解一下他说了什么。他说测试驱动开发会导致测试引起的损伤。这是他的观点。我可没说这是我的观点，这是他的观点。让我们来理解一下他说的“测试引起的损伤”是什么意思。这里有一个叫 CapacityChecker 的类，用来检查餐厅预订系统的容纳能力。

cues.en: So this is nice testable C sharp code. We have a class called capacity checker. It implements an interface called I capacity checker.
cues.zh: 这是一段非常易于测试的 C# 代码。我们定义了一个名为 CapacityChecker 的类，它实现了一个名为 ICapacityChecker 的接口。

cues.en: It uses dependency injection to have a capacity, that's just an integer, but also an IReservationRepository, and we'll need to have the constructor in order to inject those in and save them in fields for later usage. Then we have on the bottom here, hasCapacity, which is the actual value that this class provides. It says, well, given a reservation, do we have capacity, yes or no, true or false?
cues.zh: 它使用依赖注入传入一个容量值——也就是一个整数，以及一个 IReservationRepository；我们需要通过构造函数注入它们，并存入字段供后续使用。最下面是 HasCapacity 方法，这才是该类真正提供的价值。它的意思是：给定一个预约，我们是否有剩余容量，是还是否，true 还是 false？

cues.en: So what we do here on the last two lines of code there, we say, well, we'll ask the repository to get the number of reserved Cs for that date. That gives us a number of reserved Cs. Reserved is just an integer. And then we say, then we just do a comparison, you know, a less than comparison, and says, well, if the capacity is less than that, you know, what we already have reserved plus what is being requested, then the answer is false, otherwise it's true. So David Heinemeier Hansen's point here would be,
cues.zh: 最后两行代码做的事情就是：向仓储查询该日期的已预订座位数，得到一个已订数量，它就是一个整数。然后做个小于比较：如果总容量小于“已订数量加上本次申请数量”，结果就返回 false，否则返回 true。所以 David Heinemeier Hansson 的观点会是：

cues.en: Why would you ever write code like that? The only valuable thing here are those two lines of code in the bottom. The rest is just noise. Why would you do that? And then you say, well, because of testability. All right, fair enough. So I'm not even saying that this is bad in the sense that if you ask me to write a
cues.zh: 你到底为什么要写成这样？整段代码唯一有价值的，就是底部那两行，其余全是噪音。你图什么呢？然后你会说：为了可测试性啊。行吧，没毛病。我甚至不是说这种写法有多差，毕竟如果你让我用 C# 写一个

cues.en: non-trivial maintainable system in C sharp that has, you know, test coverage. This is what I do because I don't know of a better way of doing it in C sharp. So I'm not really pointing fingers at, you know, this is, I'm not saying this is bad practice. You may need to do this, but that is, that is a high cost to pay to have, you know, testability because that really, it, it, it causes your code to be spread out instead of being, you know,
cues.zh: 有测试覆盖率、非玩具级的可维护系统，我也只能这么写，因为在 C# 里我也不知道更好的办法了。所以我不是在指责这种做法，我也不是说这是坏实践。你可能不得不这么做，但为了可测试性，代价未免太高了；因为这真的会让你的代码变得很分散，而不是

cues.zh: 失败结果以及关于失败原因的更多信息；如果布尔求值结果为 true，则返回成功。所以如果我只想做得和之前完全一样、只返回一个布尔值，其实两行代码就能搞定，但这里写成了四行。除此之外，它的本质是完全一样的，这就是一个名为 check 的函数，接收三个参数。

cues.en: So what you often see in functional programming is that you'll see functions taking other functions as argument. This is what we call higher order functions. This is a completely normal thing to do. Now getReserveSeeds is a function. It plays the exact same role as that repository that you saw before. So on the first line, you can see it says letReserveSeeds equal getReserveSeedsReservation.date. That is a function call. I'm calling the function getReserveSeeds with the reservation state.
cues.zh: 在函数式编程中，你经常会看到函数将其他函数作为参数接收，这就是所谓的高阶函数，这是非常普遍的做法；现在 getReserveSeeds 是个函数，它的作用和大家之前看到的仓储完全一样；所以在第一行，你可以看到 let reservedSeats = getReserveSeeds reservation.date，这就是一次函数调用，我正在用 reservation 的日期来调用 getReserveSeeds 函数。

cues.en: And I'm getting out of that function called the number of already reserved seats. That function is just being passed in. And it's sort of polymorphic, because I'm not asking for a specific function. I'm just asking for a function that can take a data's input and give me an integer's output. Any function that can do that fits that description, and that will compile. Now, is this function that we're looking at here, is that pure or impure? It turns out to be important in just a moment.
cues.zh: 我从这次函数调用中拿到了已被预订的座位数；这个函数只是被传了进来，它有点多态的意味，因为我并没有要求特定的函数，我只要求一个能接收日期作为输入、并返回整数作为输出的函数；任何符合这一描述的函数都可以，而且能够编译通过；那么，我们眼前这个函数是纯函数还是非纯函数呢？这点马上就会变得很重要。

cues.en: So, therefore, the question. Is this pure or impure? Well, it turns out that most of the stuff that goes on up here is actually pure. The only thing we don't really know about is we don't know what get reserve seeds actually does. So it may be pure, it may be impure. Now, if get reserve seeds is sort of like the repository, like it's actually querying a database to get the number of already reserved seeds, that's an impure operation because it's not deterministic. It depends on the state of the database.
cues.zh: 所以问题来了：这是纯函数还是非纯函数？事实证明，这里进行的大部分操作其实都是纯的；我们唯一不太清楚的是，并不了解 getReserveSeeds 具体做了什么；所以它可能是纯的，也可能是非纯的；如果 getReserveSeeds 有点像仓储，比如它真的去查询数据库来获取已预订座位数，那就是非纯操作，因为它不是确定性的，它取决于数据库的状态。

cues.en: So in that case, it would be impure, and if it's impure, if that is a database code, then all of this function also becomes impure. That's how it works in F sharp. On the other hand, if getReserveCets is a pure function, then this function is also pure, because there's nothing else in that implementation that could make it impure. Why is that interesting? It's interesting because it turns out that pure functions are always testable.
cues.zh: 所以在那种情况下，它就是非纯的；如果它是非纯的，如果那是数据库调用，那么整个函数也就变成了非纯函数，F# 就是这样运作的；另一方面，如果 getReserveSeeds 是个纯函数，那么这个函数也就是纯函数，因为实现中没有其他任何东西会让它变成非纯；为什么这很有意思？有意思的地方在于，事实证明纯函数总是可测试的。

cues.en: And I'll get back to why that is, but let's just look at what would a test look like. What would a unit test look like of this function? Here's just one example. I'm only going to show you one example just to give you an idea about it. So the scenario here is that I want to test that it returns the correct result if there are no prior reservations in the system.
cues.zh: 稍后我会回过头来解释原因，不过我们先来看看测试会长什么样；这个函数的单元测试会是什么样的呢？这只是一个例子，我只给大家展示一个例子，让大家有个直观的感受；这里的场景是，我想测试在系统内没有先前预订的情况下，它是否能返回正确的结果。

cues.en: So the system just booted up. There are absolutely no reservations. The restaurant just opened. And I want to check the first reservation that comes into the system. That's basically the scenario here. So I'm saying, well, I need to set up a little bit of context. I need to define what the context is. So I say, well, what's the capacity of the restaurant? I'm just hard coding that, in this case, to 10. Because, well, that's just an easy number to think about. I like the number 10 and the number 1 and so on.
cues.zh: 也就是说系统刚刚启动，完全没有任何预订，餐厅刚刚开业；我想检查进入系统的第一笔预订，基本就是这样一个场景；所以我说，好吧，我需要设置一点上下文，需要定义一下上下文是什么；于是我说，餐厅的容量是多少？在本例中我直接把它硬编码为 10；因为这只是个便于思考的数字，我喜欢 10 和 1 之类的数字。

cues.en: So that's just arbitrary, but it's just to have a test case. Then on the next line, I say, let getReserveSeeds underscore equal zero. The underscore means that I don't care about the input. This is a local function. This is a function that only belongs to this test case. But it always returns zero, no matter what the input is.
cues.zh: 这里是随便写的，纯粹是为了凑一个测试用例。接下来这行，我写了 let getReserveSeats _ = 0。下划线表示我不关心输入。这是一个局部函数，只属于这个测试用例。但无论输入什么，它总是返回 0。

cues.en: That is a pure function because it is as deterministic as possible. It always returns zero. That means there are never any reserve seats in this particular scenario. That's a pure function. And then I have this let reservation and then a lot of crap with a lot of stuff. Yes, by the way, this is my email address. All the spammers already have it, so you might as well get it as well.
cues.zh: 这就是纯函数，因为它是完全确定性的。它始终返回 0，意味着在这个特定场景下永远没有预留座位。这就是纯函数。然后我有这个 let reservation，接着是一大堆杂七杂八的东西。顺便说一句，这是我的邮箱地址，垃圾邮件发送者早就全有了，你们知道也无妨。

cues.en: So that's just, you know, that's a little bit, that looks a little noisy because there's actually a lot of code there, but it's just data, and we could put that in some sort of factory if we wanted to do that, but I'm just showing you a self-contained example here. And then, you know, on the third to last line there, it says let actual equal capacity check, capacity get reserve seed preservation. I'm taking those three arguments that I set up in a range phase and just passing them as arguments, I'm getting an actual result back.
cues.zh: 看起来有点乱，因为代码确实挺多的，但这只是数据，真想写的话也可以放进工厂函数里，不过我这里只是想展示一个自包含的例子。然后倒数第三行写着 let actual = capacityCheck capacity getReserveSeats reservation。我把准备阶段设置的那三个参数传进去，拿到了实际的返回结果。

cues.en: And I can now declare what did I expect and compare those two things to each other. And this test will either pass or fail. That was easy. So you might wonder now, is it coincidental that this was easy to test? And it turns out it's not. There is a reason why this was easy to write. And the reason is that as long as a function is pure, it is intrinsically testable. And let's try to understand why that is. In order to get help,
cues.zh: 现在我可以声明预期结果，并将两者进行对比。测试要么通过，要么失败。这很容易。你现在可能会想，这么容易测试难道只是巧合吗？事实并非如此。之所以这么容易写是有原因的，原因就是只要一个函数是纯函数，它就天生具备可测试性。我们试着理解一下为什么会这样。为了搞清楚这点，

cues.en: to understand that. Let's refer to Jessica Kerr. Jessica Kerr sometimes talks about a concept that she calls isolation. And she says, isolation is, you know, when the only information a function has about the external world is something that is passed into it via arguments, then the function has isolation. And that is a good thing, by the way. This is, you know, a desirable quality of a function.
cues.zh: 我们需要参考一下 Jessica Kerr 的观点。Jessica Kerr 有时会提到一个她称之为“隔离”的概念。她说所谓的隔离，就是当一个函数对外部世界的唯一认知仅来自于通过参数传入的内容时，这个函数就具备隔离性。顺便说一句，这是件好事，是函数非常可取的品质。

cues.en: So, basically what we're saying is a function does not have any implicit knowledge about the outside world. Everything it needs to know in order to do what it is that it wants to do needs to be passed in as arguments. Now, is a pure function isolated? Yes, always, because a pure function
cues.zh: 基本上也就是说，函数对外部世界没有任何隐式认知。它为了完成自身功能所需的一切信息，都必须作为参数传入。那么纯函数具备隔离性吗？是的，绝对具备，因为纯函数

cues.en: It must be deterministic. Otherwise, it's not pure. And by deterministic, we're saying it should always return the same output given the same input. It is only the input that can influence the output of a function. So therefore, a pure function is a subset of all functions that have isolation. The F sharp function that I just showed you may not be pure. We talked about that. But it has isolation because it makes no attempt of
cues.zh: 必须是确定性的，否则就不是纯函数。所谓确定性，是指在给定相同输入的情况下，它必须总是返回相同的输出。只有输入才能影响函数的输出。因此，纯函数是所有具备隔离性函数的一个子集。我刚才展示的 F# 函数可能不是纯函数，我们之前讨论过。但它具备隔离性，因为它完全没有试图

cues.en: using implicit knowledge about the world. Everything it tries to do is based on its function argument. So it has isolation. It may not be pure. Maybe it is. We don't know. But at least pure functions, the ideal of functional programming, all pure functions have isolation. Why is isolation interesting? Let's talk about unit testing. Why is isolation important in the context of unit testing? Well,
cues.zh: 利用对外部世界的隐式认知。它尝试做的一切都基于它的函数参数。所以它具备隔离性。它可能不是纯函数，也可能是，我们不确定。但至少纯函数——函数式编程的理想形态——所有纯函数都具备隔离性。为什么隔离性很有意思？我们来聊聊单元测试。为什么隔离性在单元测试的语境下如此重要？

cues.en: Let's try to see if we can come up with a definition of unit testing. Basically, if you have 10 experts in unit testing and you ask them to come up with a definition of what a unit test is, you'll get 12 answers.
cues.zh: 我们试着给单元测试下个定义。基本上，找 10 个单元测试专家让他们给单元测试下定义，你能得到 12 种答案。

cues.en: So it's not really possible to get one definition of a unit test. But here's one that I use. A unit test is an automated test that tests a unit in isolation from its dependencies. And most experts in unit testing, where they disagree is where all the controversy is. It means it's basically around what is a unit. And I'm not particularly interested in what a unit is.
cues.zh: 其实很难对单元测试下一个统一定义。但我常用的是这个：单元测试是一种自动化测试，用于将某个单元与其依赖项隔离开来单独测试。而大多数单元测试专家的分歧和所有争议的核心，基本上都围绕着“什么是单元”。我对什么是单元并不是特别感兴趣。

cues.en: The thing that I'm interested in in this definition is the word isolation. We want to test the unit in isolation of its dependencies. This is the same sort of isolation that Jessica Carr talks about. All right. So let's try to understand why, you know, why David Heinemeier Hansen may be up onto something and why it's not a concern in functional programming. So David Heinemeier Hansen says, well, isolation is an important quality of your code if you want it to be testable.
cues.zh: 在这个定义中，我真正感兴趣的是“隔离”这个词。我们希望把单元从它的依赖项中隔离开来测试。这和 Jessica Kerr 所谈论的隔离是同一种类型。好，那我们试着来理解一下，为什么 David Heinemeier Hansson 的观点可能有些道理，以及为什么这在函数式编程中不是个问题。David Heinemeier Hansson 说过，如果想要代码具备可测试性，隔离就是一个非常重要的特性。

cues.en: And then, you know, you try to combine that with object-oriented programming, and bang, you have test-induced damage. And I think that David Heinemeier has drawn the wrong conclusion. He says, and that's the fault of test-driven development. Whereas I'm more and more beginning to see, I can do test-driven development with functional programming, and it does not lead to test-induced damage. So therefore, the problem must be somewhere else. And I think actually OOP is the problem.
cues.zh: 然后，当你试图把这一点和面向对象编程结合起来时，砰的一声，你就得到了“测试诱发的破坏”。我认为 David Heinemeier 得出了错误的结论。他说，这是测试驱动开发的错。但我越来越清晰地意识到，我可以用函数式编程来做测试驱动开发，而且它完全不会导致测试诱发的破坏。所以，问题肯定出在别的地方。我认为实际上 OOP 才是问题所在。

cues.en: So let's try to understand why object-oriented programming is a problem here. Now, the ideal, the design ideal, the philosophy behind OOP is encapsulation. This is what we're aiming for. This is what we were taught is important in object-oriented design. If we want to be testable, we now need to aim for this quality of isolation, because otherwise it's not really testable.
cues.zh: 那么让我们来看看，为什么面向对象编程会在这里成为问题。面向对象背后的设计理念、哲学是封装。这是我们的终极目标，也是我们在面向对象设计中被教导要重视的东西。而如果我们想要代码可测试，我们现在就必须追求这种“隔离”的特性，否则代码就谈不上真正的可测试。

cues.en: Now, again, we're in this situation where we're trying to roll a boulder up the hill. It is possible to sit there in the intersection between those two, you know, sets and say, here's testable OOD. It is possible. But again, you know, it requires a lot of effort and it requires a lot of diligence and a lot of, you know, constant monitoring of what's going on because otherwise you would probably add to one of the sides.
cues.zh: 现在，我们又陷入了这种像推巨石上山一样的境地。坐在那两个集合的交集里说“这就是可测试的 OOD”，确实是可能的。完全做得到。但同样，这需要付出极大的努力，需要极度用心，并持续监控各种情况，否则你很可能会偏向其中一边。

cues.en: And what's often happening is if you don't have a focus on test driven development or testability, you may add to the side of encapsulation. That's basically what happened the first 10 years of the .NET framework, for example.
cues.zh: 通常会发生的情况是，如果你不重视测试驱动开发或可测试性，你就可能会偏向封装那一侧。比如，.NET framework 最初的 10 年基本上就是这么回事。

cues.en: The first 10 years of the base class library in .NET, it was infamous for not being particularly testable. It's much better now, but it was really difficult to test base class libraries the first 10 years of the .NET framework's lifetime. Now, on the other hand, if you are focusing on test-driven development, you often err to the side of isolation. And then you get something that has this test-induced damage that David Heinemeihansen talks about.
cues.zh: .NET 基础类库最初的 10 年，就是因为极其不便测试而臭名昭著。现在好多了，但在 .NET framework 诞生的前 10 年里，基础类库真的很难做测试。而另一方面，如果你一心专注于测试驱动开发，你往往会偏向隔离那一侧。于是就会出现 David Heinemeier Hansson 所说的这种“测试诱发的破坏”。

cues.en: functional programming is different. Because what's the ideal function in functional programming? Well, it's that pure function that we already talked about. That is the design ideal. It has isolation. And because it has isolation, it's testable. There may be other ways to make things testable. But if they have isolation, they tend to be testable. But there's no intersection that you need to fit into. Basically, if I had a team of...
cues.zh: 函数式编程则不同。因为函数式编程中理想的函数是什么样的？就是我们刚才谈到的纯函数。那是设计的理想境界。它具有隔离性。正因为具备隔离性，它才是可测试的。让代码具备可测试性可能还有别的方法，但只要具备隔离性，往往就很容易测试。而且你不需要去迎合各种重叠的要求。基本上，如果我有一支……

cues.en: developers who are already good at doing functional programming, I could basically just say to them, if I was the lead developer or software architect, I could say, just write as many pure functions as you can. Do good functional programming design. Write pure functions. And I'll go on holiday, and I'll come back, and then we'll see. Then we can start testing it. That might actually be possible, because if they write pure functions, they are testable.
cues.zh: 熟练掌握函数式编程的开发团队，如果我是主程序员或软件架构师，我基本上可以直接对他们说，尽量多写纯函数。做好函数式编程的设计，写出纯函数来。然后我就去度假，等我回来后再看，到时候我们就可以开始测试了。这完全是有可能的，因为只要他们写的是纯函数，代码就是可测试的。

cues.en: So what I'm trying to do here in this talk is to talk about, in my experience, there were lots of things, more than three things, that I've experienced during my career as architect and lead developer and so on, where I say, this requires a lot of effort. This is really difficult to do in C sharp and probably also in Java. But it turns out that if I try to rephrase the way that I approach my things and use functional programming instead, all of these things just sort of automatically...
cues.zh: 所以，我今天演讲的目的是想分享一下我的经验。在我的架构师和主程序员等职业生涯中，经历过很多事情，远不止三件，我常觉得“这需要付出巨大的努力”，“这在 C# 里真的很难实现，在 Java 里大概也一样”。但事实证明，如果我尝试换个思路，改用函数式编程，所有这些问题都会自然而然地……

cues.en: fall into a successful place. It just automatically happens. So we looked at three things. We looked at ports and adapters. We looked at services, entities, and value objects. We looked at testability. All of these things turn out to work very well. It's not the only three I know of others, but I didn't have time to describe any more. If you want to know more, then...
